Read a diagram of two rows of plant cups and say which four plants each child of the class looks after.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/kindergarten-garden) (MIT). Listed under [Grids & Matrices](/examples/?subject=grids-and-matrices).

```nomi-run
// FILE: kindergarten_garden.nomi
//# Which plants each child of a kindergarten class looks after, from a
//# diagram of the cups on the windowsill.

/// A plant grown in the class's garden.
pub enum Plant {
    Grass
    Clover
    Radishes
    Violets
}

impl Plant {
    /// The plant a diagram writes as `letter`, or `None` for a letter that
    /// names no plant.
    pub fn from_letter(letter: String) -> Maybe<Plant> {
        case letter {
            "G" -> Some(.Grass)
            "C" -> Some(.Clover)
            "R" -> Some(.Radishes)
            "V" -> Some(.Violets)
            _ -> None
        }
    }
}

/// A child of the class, in the alphabetical order cups are handed out.
pub enum Student {
    Alice
    Bob
    Charlie
    David
    Eve
    Fred
    Ginny
    Harriet
    Ileana
    Joseph
    Kincaid
    Larry
}

derive Variants for Student

/// Two rows of cups, the row nearest the window first.
pub opaque struct Garden {
    rows: List<List<Plant>>
}

impl Garden {
    /// Reads a diagram of one line per row of cups, or `None` when a letter
    /// names no plant.
    pub fn parse(diagram: String) -> Maybe<Garden> {
        diagram
        |> String.lines()
        |> Iter.map(parse_row)
        |> Maybe.collect()
        |> Maybe.map(&#Garden{rows: &1})
    }

    /// The plants in `student`'s cups: two in each row, left to right, the
    /// row nearest the window first.
    pub fn plants(garden: Garden, student: Student) -> List<Plant> {
        first_cup = 2 * position(student)

        garden.rows
        |> Iter.flat_map(fn row -> row |> Iter.drop(first_cup) |> Iter.take(2))
        |> Iter.to_list()
    }
}

fn parse_row(row: String) -> Maybe<List<Plant>> {
    row
    |> Iter.map(Plant.from_letter)
    |> Maybe.collect()
}

/// How many students come before `student` in the class. Every student is
/// in `Student.variants()`, so the search cannot miss.
fn position(student: Student) -> Int {
    Some(i) = Student.variants() |> Iter.find_index(&(&1 == student)) else {
        unreachable "every student is listed"
    }
    i
}

// FILE: kindergarten_garden_test.nomi
import kindergarten_garden.{Garden, Plant, Student}

group "partial garden" {
    test "plants" {
        cases = [
            #(
                "garden with single student",
                "RC\nGG",
                Student.Alice,
                [Plant.Radishes, .Clover, .Grass, .Grass],
            ),
            #(
                "different garden with single student",
                "VC\nRC",
                .Alice,
                [.Violets, .Clover, .Radishes, .Clover],
            ),
            #(
                "garden with two students",
                "VVCG\nVVRC",
                .Bob,
                [.Clover, .Grass, .Radishes, .Clover],
            ),
        ]

        subtests cases, #(description, diagram, student, expected), description {
            assert Some(garden) = Garden.parse(diagram)

            assert Garden.plants(garden, student) == expected
        }
    }

    test "multiple students for the same garden with three students" {
        garden = try Garden.parse("VVCCGG\nVVCCGG")

        cases = [
            #("second student's garden", Student.Bob, [Plant.Clover, .Clover, .Clover, .Clover]),
            #("third student's garden", .Charlie, [.Grass, .Grass, .Grass, .Grass]),
        ]

        subtests cases, #(description, student, expected), description {
            assert Garden.plants(garden, student) == expected
        }
    }
}

test "full garden" {
    garden = try Garden.parse("VRCGVVRVCGGCCGVRGCVCGCGV\nVRCCCGCRRGVCGCRVVCVGCGCV")

    cases = [
        #(
            "for Alice, first student's garden",
            Student.Alice,
            [Plant.Violets, .Radishes, .Violets, .Radishes],
        ),
        #("for Bob, second student's garden", .Bob, [.Clover, .Grass, .Clover, .Clover]),
        #("for Charlie", .Charlie, [.Violets, .Violets, .Clover, .Grass]),
        #("for David", .David, [.Radishes, .Violets, .Clover, .Radishes]),
        #("for Eve", .Eve, [.Clover, .Grass, .Radishes, .Grass]),
        #("for Fred", .Fred, [.Grass, .Clover, .Violets, .Clover]),
        #("for Ginny", .Ginny, [.Clover, .Grass, .Grass, .Clover]),
        #("for Harriet", .Harriet, [.Violets, .Radishes, .Radishes, .Violets]),
        #("for Ileana", .Ileana, [.Grass, .Clover, .Violets, .Clover]),
        #("for Joseph", .Joseph, [.Violets, .Clover, .Violets, .Grass]),
        #(
            "for Kincaid, second to last student's garden",
            .Kincaid,
            [.Grass, .Clover, .Clover, .Grass],
        ),
        #("for Larry, last student's garden", .Larry, [.Grass, .Violets, .Clover, .Violets]),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, student, expected), description {
        assert Garden.plants(garden, student) == expected
    }
}

test "a letter that names no plant" {
    assert Garden.parse("VX\nRC") == None
}
```

## How it's written

- Plants and students are enums. The class is fixed at twelve named children, so asking for a child who is not in it cannot be written, and `Garden.plants` needs no error.
- The diagram is parsed once into an opaque `Garden` by `Garden.parse`, which returns `None` for a letter that names no plant. A diagram is data, so a bad one is an answer rather than a trap. The canonical data has no bad diagram; the test file adds one, marked as not canonical.
- A student's position is their index in `derive Variants`' list (`Iter.find_index`), so the alphabetical order lives only in the enum's declaration. Every student is in that list, so the search cannot miss: its `None` is `unreachable "every student is listed"` (style §28), a trap if the enum and the list ever disagree, rather than a default that would answer a wrong position.
- `Garden.plants` takes two cups from each row with `Iter.drop` and `Iter.take` under one `Iter.flat_map`.
- "partial garden" is a `group` of its two tests, the nested canonical group "multiple students for the same garden with three students" among them, since groups do not nest; "full garden" is a plain test. Where every row shares a diagram, the test parses it once with `try` before the table; where rows bring their own, the row parses it with `assert Some(garden) = ...`, since `try` cannot be used in a `subtests` body.
- Each table's first row qualifies its variants (`Student.Alice`, `[Plant.Radishes, ...]`), and the later rows write them bare.
